title: 📋 IELTS Test Format — Complete Overview

sections.heading: The four skills
sections.body:
🎧 LISTENING (30 min + 10 min transfer)
4 sections, 40 questions, increasing difficulty
Sections 1–2: everyday, Sections 3–4: academic

👁️ READING (60 min)
3 passages, 40 questions
Academic: complex texts from books/journals
General: notices, adverts, workplace documents

✍️ WRITING (60 min)
Task 1 (20 min): 150+ words — describe data/diagram
Task 2 (40 min): 250+ words — essay

🗣️ SPEAKING (11–14 min)
Part 1: Introduction (4–5 min)
Part 2: Cue card long turn (3–4 min)
Part 3: Abstract discussion (4–5 min)

sections.heading: Scoring
sections.body:
Each skill is scored 1–9 in 0.5 increments.
Overall band = average of 4 skills (rounded to nearest 0.5)

Band 9: Expert user
Band 8: Very good user
Band 7: Good user
Band 6: Competent user
Band 5: Modest user

highlight: Academic vs General Training: They differ in Reading and Writing Task 1. Speaking and Listening are the SAME for both. Check which version your institution requires.

instruction: Match each IELTS section to its correct time:
explanation: Total test time ≈ 2 hours 45 minutes (not counting speaking, which is on a different day at most test centres).

question: How is the IELTS overall band score calculated?
options: The average of all four section scores
The combined total of all scores divided by 2
correct: The average of all four section scores
explanation:
Overall Band = (Listening + Reading + Writing + Speaking) ÷ 4, rounded to nearest 0.5

Example: 7.0 + 6.5 + 6.0 + 7.0 = 26.5 ÷ 4 = 6.625 → rounded to 6.5

This means a very weak skill CAN bring down your overall score significantly — you can't compensate with one strong skill.

question: What is the key difference between Academic and General Training IELTS?
options: The Listening test uses different accents
Reading passages and Writing Task 1 are different
correct: Reading passages and Writing Task 1 are different
explanation:
Academic IELTS:
• Reading: complex academic texts from journals/books
• Writing Task 1: describe a graph, chart, diagram, or map

General Training IELTS:
• Reading: practical texts — notices, job ads, workplace documents
• Writing Task 1: write a letter (formal, semi-formal, or informal)

Listening and Speaking are identical for both.

sentence: In the IELTS Speaking test, Part 2 requires candidates to speak for _______ to _______ minutes on a given topic.
explanation:
Part 2: Speak for 1–2 minutes after 1 minute of preparation.

You should aim to speak for the full 2 minutes — stopping early signals running out of ideas.
The examiner stops you if you go over 2 minutes.
